steps.description: Filter genes with filterByExpr (edgeR) requiring at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size (60), then TMM-normalize with edgeR::calcNormFactors. Build design matrix ~condition with control as the explicit reference level. Run limma-voom with precision weights as the primary fixed-effects test (this is the primary model, chosen over DESeq2/edgeR NB models because population-cohort sample variation departs from the negative-binomial assumption at n>=50/group, causing exaggerated false positives even under permuted labels). In parallel, run a Wilcoxon rank-sum test per gene on normalized log-CPM values as a non-parametric robustness control and report the overlap between the two gene lists. Separately, also fit a DESeq2 NB model (median-of-ratios normalization, default outlier replacement via Cook's distance since n>=7/group) purely to obtain a coefficient for apeglm shrinkage in the next step — this DESeq2 fit is not the inferential test, only the shrinkage input.

steps.description: Apply apeglm log2 fold-change shrinkage to the companion DESeq2 fit from T1S2 to obtain a noise-reduced effect size per gene, reported alongside the unshrunken limma-voom log2FC and its standard error. Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment (alpha=0.05) to the limma-voom moderated-t p-values with independent filtering, and separately run a TREAT-style test (limma::treat / DESeq2 lfcThreshold with apeglm shrinkage for the posterior) against an explicitly stated log2 fold-change threshold (0.5, i.e. ~1.4-fold) so that the 'large enough to matter' claim is a formal test against a threshold rather than a post-hoc filter on the point estimate. plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE (n=60/60) with effect-size focus
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a large population-scale bulk RNA-seq cohort (60 cases vs 60 controls, whole blood, single batch, unpaired, 12000 genes x 121 samples from raw Salmon gene-level counts). At n=60/group the knowledge base flags that count-based negative binomial models (DESeq2/edgeR) exaggerate false positives in population cohorts because sample-to-sample variation departs from the NB assumption even under permuted labels (Mishra et al. 2022, doi:10.1186/s13059-022-02648-4). The primary inferential test is therefore limma-voom with TMM normalization and a fixed-effects linear model, with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test run in parallel as a distribution-free robustness check. Because the research question explicitly separates statistical significance from effect-size magnitude ('large enough to matter, not only significant'), the plan reports shrunken log2 fold changes (apeglm, run on a companion DESeq2 fit since limma has no shrinkage estimator) alongside the limma moderated-t results, and applies a TREAT/lfcThreshold test against a stated fold-change threshold rather than a post-hoc filter on the point estimate. Multiple testing uses BH-FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05. Enrichment runs on the full ranked gene list (moderated t-statistic) with camera (accounts for inter-gene correlation, appropriate at this sample size) and fgsea preranked, against the locally available MSigDB Hallmark set first, then Reactome as the confirmatory second collection; over-representation analysis is explicitly avoided unless the significant gene list exceeds ~50 genes. The report step consolidates diagnostics (p-value histogram, MA/mean-difference plot), lists genes passing both FDR and effect-size thresholds, reports the DE-model vs Wilcoxon-control overlap, and states all thresholds, package versions, and gene-set collection versions for reproducibility.
